examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: For deletion, identify whether a predecessor is available and handle head/tail cases. Given only a node in a singly linked list, deleting the tail still requires finding its predecessor. A loop testing current->next never examines the original head. After removal, keep the predecessor in place to catch consecutive matches.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
In list 1→2→2→3, retain the head and repeatedly delete its current successor when that successor is 2. How many reachable nodes remain?

**Answer: 2.** Remove the first 2 after head 1, then inspect the new successor and remove the second 2. Retain 3. The final list is 1→3, with two nodes.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
Unlinking does not automatically free memory. A production deletion routine must manage ownership and update external head/tail pointers.

Constant-time insertion assumes the insertion position is already known; finding it can cost Θ(n).
